q: Does a CPCB red category factory have high carbon emissions?
title: CPCB red category and carbon
short: Not necessarily. CPCB colour categories rank industries by pollution potential, such as air and water pollutants and hazardous waste, not by greenhouse gases. A red category unit may have modest CO2, and a green category unit with a big boiler or many kilns can emit more. Measure CO2 from your fuel and power bills.

ul: Red, orange, green and white come from a pollution index set by CPCB.
They decide consent conditions and inspection frequency.
They say nothing about your Scope 1 and 2 total.

sections.h: What buyers and lenders ask instead
p: They ask for tonnes of CO2e from fuel and electricity, with the documents behind them, and sometimes for Scope 3.

senseible: Senseible reads bills, fuel invoices and production records into dated, fingerprinted records, so the figure you send a buyer can be traced to its documents.
